findings.title: Verification accepts missing artifacts and nonexistent source commits
findings.detail: approveReview checks only the shape of artifact SHA256 values and sourceRevision. Neither verify nor load reads handoff artifact bytes or resolves the source commit. A matching review can therefore mark a task VERIFIED and unlock successors even when its evidence file does not exist or its source commit is nonexistent. This violates the promised committed-source/evidence gate and leaves subsequent artifact drift undetected.
reproduction: Create an isolated schedulerStore fixture with VL-001 and a dependent VL-002, plus real agent1/agent2 ownership and runtime directories, as in tests/governance/desktop-scheduler.test.mjs.

Reserve/start VL-001 with actual ec80cec source. Submit acceptanceMet:true, command exitCode:0, and artifacts:[{ref:'does-not-exist.json',sha256:'a'.repeat(64)}]. Write an APPROVED agent2 review bound to the exact handoff hash and ec80cec source. store.verify and store.load both succeed; VL-001 becomes VERIFIED and VL-002 READY.

In the isolated fixture, use sourceRevision:'f'.repeat(40), a real package.json artifact with its actual hash, and a review matching the new handoff/source. git cat-file confirms that source is not a commit, yet store.verify and store.load succeed.
findings.requestedChange: Before VERIFIED, resolve the exact committed source and validate safe artifact references and actual SHA256 bytes, including binding tracked source/evidence artifacts to the submitted commit. Fail closed on missing, mismatched or escaping evidence and on later drift during load. Add isolated negative regressions. Preserve the old source/handoff/review when resubmitting.
